parsed.doc_summary: Massachusetts Landlords association article: under G.L. c.186 §15B landlords may only require first, last, security deposit and lock charges before tenancy; application fees forbidden for lessors, but licensed brokers may charge fees under 254 CMR 7 with written disclosure.

rules.title: MA limit on upfront charges by lessors (no application fees)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a landlord may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock charge. Application, screening, pet, cleaning or amenity fees charged by a landlord are forbidden.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, security deposit, and lock
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks (MGL Ch 186 Section 15B).
rules.effective_date_note: Article says the law has been in effect since the 1970s; no exact date given.
rules.exemptions: Licensed brokers may charge fees under 254 CMR 7.
rules.interaction: Brokers are treated differently from lessors.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source; broker/landlord-as-broker status is uncertain.
rules.penalty: Treble damages and attorney's fees (per Perry v. Equity Residential, federal district court).

rules.title: MA licensed broker fee disclosure regulation
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees, but must give written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on a lease, signed by the applicant, at the first personal meeting.
rules.key_value: Written broker fee disclosure at first personal meeting
rules.quoted_span: the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to licensed brokers dealing with prospective tenants.
